hunt.justification: Identity is the primary attack surface in 2026; Business Email Compromise (BEC) costs organizations more than ransomware. Detecting the gap between a successful login and the abuse of SaaS configuration is the most effective way to prevent financial fraud.

scenario.summary: In 2026, attackers are increasingly leveraging AI-powered phishing and the hijacking of trusted RMM tools like ScreenConnect to establish stealthy persistence. These campaigns often transition to identity-centric attacks, bypassing MFA via session theft and manipulating cloud environments through BEC flows, ultimately culminating in data exfiltration and multi-extortion ransomware.

meta.rationale: Prioritize users with 'privileged' roles or those in finance/HR departments. Focus on the last 14 days to capture active BEC campaigns.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary has bypassed MFA via session hijacking or proxy usage and is establishing persistence through malicious inbox rules or unauthorized OAuth applications in a SaaS environment.

blind_spots.risk: Attackers can hide their source IP without detection if the IDP does not provide proxy intelligence.
blind_spots.question: whether a login originated from an anonymizing proxy
blind_spots.requires: is_proxy field populated by the identity provider (e.g., Okta)
blind_spots.remediation: Enable IP threat intelligence and proxy detection within the IDP settings.

blind_spots.risk: A 24-hour log delay means an attacker can exfiltrate data and establish persistence before the hunt even sees the API call.
blind_spots.question: how quickly persistence can be established after a compromise
blind_spots.remediation: Move M365 log ingestion to a high-priority stream (e.g., Office 365 Management Activity API directly).

hunt.name: Identity Compromise and SaaS Persistence
hunt.description: This hunt identifies successful logins that bypass security controls (proxies, MFA failure) and correlates them with downstream SaaS persistence mechanisms. It uses three telemetry surfaces—identity logs, API activity, and geolocational stack-counting—to separate legitimate remote work from Business Email Compromise (BEC). The agent weighs the login context against the creation of inbox rules or OAuth grants to confirm active account takeover.

nodes.label: Successful logins via proxies or without MFA

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, src_location_country, src_location_city, mfa, is_proxy, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND (is_proxy = 'true' OR mfa = 'false') AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify initial access leads where authentication succeeded but bypassed typical security postures.
config.expected_signal: Rows identify users and IPs that authenticated through known proxies or without MFA. Silence indicates no obvious bypasses in the monitored telemetry.

primitive_config.label: Successful logins via proxies or without MFA
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_endpoint_ip, src_location_country, src_location_city, mfa, is_proxy, time FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND (is_proxy = 'true' OR mfa = 'false') AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Rows identify users and IPs that authenticated through known proxies or without MFA. Silence indicates no obvious bypasses in the monitored telemetry.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_location_country, src_location_city, COUNT(DISTINCT src_endpoint_ip) AS unique_ips, MIN(time) AS first_login, MAX(time) AS last_login FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_location_country, src_location_city HAVING unique_ips < 3 ORDER BY unique_ips ASC
config.description: Highlight 'impossible travel' or unusual login origins by identifying locations seen on fewer than three IPs per user.
config.expected_signal: Rare combinations of user and location. A single row for a user in a new country is a strong indicator of session theft or unauthorized access.

primitive_config.label: Stack-count login locations per user
primitive_config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, src_location_country, src_location_city, COUNT(DISTINCT src_endpoint_ip) AS unique_ips, MIN(time) AS first_login, MAX(time) AS last_login FROM hb_auth_signin WHERE status_id = 1 AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY actor_user_name, src_location_country, src_location_city HAVING unique_ips < 3 ORDER BY unique_ips ASC
primitive_config.expected: Rare combinations of user and location. A single row for a user in a new country is a strong indicator of session theft or unauthorized access.

config.content: SELECT actor_user_name, api_operation, resource_name, src_endpoint_ip, time FROM hb_cloud_api_activity WHERE (LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%inboxrule%' OR LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%consent%' OR LOWER(api_operation) LIKE '%oauth2permissiongrant%') AND ('{{target_users}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{target_users}}' || ',', ',' || actor_user_name || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect the technical aftermath of a successful login: inbox rule creation and OAuth app consent.
config.expected_signal: API calls that create persistence or allow data exfiltration. Common legitimate rules for folders should be manually filtered by the agent.

config.description: Correlate suspicious login leads with rare locations and SaaS-level persistence to confirm identity theft.

nodes.label: Revoke User Sessions and Reset Credentials

config.description: Evict the adversary by invalidating all current session tokens and requiring a password change with MFA re-enrollment.
config.instructions: Revoke all active sign-in sessions for the identified user(s). Force a password reset and audit MFA devices for unauthorized additions.

config.description: Review the specific inbox rules and OAuth grants to determine the scope of data theft or interception.
config.instructions: Inspect the content of the created inbox rules for financial keywords (invoice, wire, payment). Verify whether the OAuth applications have permissions to read mail or modify directory settings.

config.description: Improve detection coverage and identity hygiene based on the hunt findings.
config.instructions: Record the source IPs of the attackers for blocklisting. Update MFA policies to enforce hardware-backed or FIDO2 tokens to prevent session theft bypass. If specific inbox rules were common, promote them to standing detection rules.
